scopeReview: IMP-2.A.1–3: fertility, mortality, migration, natural increase, doubling time and social/cultural/political/economic influences. All rates and flows are hypothetical; rule70 assumptions explicit. No real policy guidance, health diagnosis or deterministic claim about a population.
varietyReview: Four interpreted stimuli separate accounting, paired rates, approximate doubling and migration direction. Other items distinguish age weights, momentum, policy opportunities versus completed flows and rate/count comparisons. All five skills, four keys and varied difficulty represented.
repetitionReview: Different from2.3 snapshot composition: measures flows, rates, projection and influences. The two natural-change tasks distinguish rate conversion from a negative-natural/positive-migration counterexample, not merely the same arithmetic with replaced numbers.

questions.correctOption: 1.4% natural increase; a net gain of 400 residents
questions.independentReview: Recomputed births−deaths1400; immigration−emigration−1000; sum400. Used100000 midyear denominator to obtain1.4% natural increase. Checked per-thousand14 versus percent1.4 and avoided assigning an unsupported end-year population.

questions.correctOption: It remains 2% in the first two periods and then falls to 1%.
questions.independentReview: Independently computed paired gaps20,20,10 per1000 and percentages2,2,1. Checked that migration is absent from natural increase and no doubling interval is provided by the chart alone.
Recomputed70/2=35 and70/1=70. Corroborated with discrete compounding ln2/ln1.02≈35.003 and ln2/ln1.01≈69.661 years; approximation errors are under one year.

questions.correctOption: Area B has a net migration gain of 2,500 residents; its total change also depends on births and deaths.
questions.independentReview: Followed actual arrow endpoints and counts: A→B3000, B→A500. Recomputed Bnet+2500 and Anet−2500, which sum0 for this closed pair, without inferring unshown birth/death balances.

questions.correctOption: The crude birth rate also reflects the population’s age composition, not only fertility behavior.
questions.independentReview: Held age-specific fertility schedules similar and varied age weights in the total population. The crude rate is a weighted population outcome and need not equal a per-woman lifetime measure.

questions.correctOption: Different age composition can raise the crude rate even when age-specific death rates are lower.
questions.independentReview: Checked the weighted-rate logic: a population concentrated in higher-mortality age groups can have a higher crude rate despite lower rates within each group. No claim about a real country or individual health diagnosis is made.

questions.correctOption: Total population rises by 1,000 despite natural decrease.
questions.independentReview: Independently added signed components−1000+2000=1000. Natural decrease and total growth are compatible under the supplied migration balance.

questions.correctOption: Population momentum can sustain substantial births as a large cohort reaches reproductive ages.
questions.independentReview: Separated lower fertility per woman from the size of the population entering childbearing ages. More potential parents can coexist with fewer births per woman; no exact future growth path is asserted.

questions.correctOption: These opportunities can influence timing and family-size decisions, without fixing an identical response for everyone.
questions.independentReview: Assessed a conditional mechanism rather than a universal claim about education, gender or employment. The hypothetical association supports investigation but not a fixed individual response or a sole-cause conclusion.

questions.correctOption: The decision may influence migration, but actual demographic flows are needed to determine total change.
questions.independentReview: Distinguished authorization/eligibility from completed movement and retained the four flow components. No real immigration law or policy outcome is asserted.
Independently multiplied.01*1000000=10000 and.02*200000=4000. Rates and absolute growth rankings differ; migration is explicitly excluded.
